scope.population: Current-serving military personnel based in Greater Darwin and their adult family members, including overseas military personnel and families living elsewhere.

sources.rand: Miller et al. (2011), A New Approach for Assessing the Needs of Service Members and Their Families, Appendix A, printed pp. 75–115; Chapter 4, pp. 37–48.
sources.strategy: Supplied Defence and Veteran Family Wellbeing Strategy 2025–2030 and First Action Plan.
sources.wording_review: Retains v3 Australian English. Funding listing, LC privacy-policy link and public feedback email, and OAIC APP 5 guidance rechecked 29 September 2026. See SOURCES.md.
sources.implementation_basis: Jacob’s latest decision: retain multiple-choice needs and follow-up; compact pages; optional 10,000-character narrative for each tracked need. No fresh GitHub checkout inspected in this preparation.

pages.title: Defence Family Support Survey
intro: Have your say and help shape a stronger Defence community in Greater Darwin.

By sharing your experiences, you can help shape support that makes everyday Defence life easier and strengthens community connections. We want to hear what has been difficult, what has helped and where support is still missing.
Lutheran Care is developing its Defence Family Support Program. Thank you for helping us understand what matters to serving members and their families.
pages.funding_acknowledgement: Lutheran Care gratefully acknowledges funding from the Australian Government Department of Defence through the Family Support Funding Program.

sections.title: Who can take part
sections.text: This questionnaire is for people aged 18 or older who are currently serving in the Australian Defence Force (ADF) or another country’s military and are based in Greater Darwin, and their adult family members. Family members may live elsewhere. Family includes partners, former partners, parents, adult children, other relatives, kin and carers.

sections.title: What to expect
sections.text: The first questions ask a little about you and which issue areas matter to you. For up to two areas, you can describe the help you needed and what happened in your own words. Each question has space for a written answer. You can write as much or as little as you like, or leave a question unanswered.

sections.title: Your choice
sections.text: Taking part is voluntary. You can skip questions, choose not to answer or stop at any time. Some questions cover health, relationships, safety and bereavement. Share only what you feel comfortable sharing. You can review and change your answers before finishing.

sections.title: Your information
sections.text: Lutheran Care will use the information you choose to share to understand local needs and plan family support. Please do not include names, street addresses, contact details, service numbers or details that could identify another person. Do not include classified or operationally sensitive information. When describing a family experience, share only what you know and do not identify the person.

sections.title: Your privacy
sections.text: Lutheran Care handles personal information under its Confidentiality and Privacy Policy. Information may be shared where required or authorised by law. The policy explains how to request access to or correction of your personal information, and how to make a privacy complaint.

sections.title: Questions or concerns
sections.text: For questions about the survey or your privacy, contact Lutheran Care at feedback@lutherancare.org.au and mention the Defence Family Support Program. Completing this survey is not an application for a service or activity.

sections.title: About this questionnaire
sections.text: This questionnaire adapts the approach and sample survey in RAND’s A New Approach for Assessing the Needs of Service Members and Their Families (2011). The issue list also draws on the Defence and Veteran Family Wellbeing Strategy 2025–2030.

pages.title: Issues in everyday life
intro: Think about the past 12 months and issues connected with your or your family’s life in Greater Darwin, including a move here. If the current posting began more recently, think about the time since it began and the move, within the past 12 months.
Include issues that have now been resolved. They do not have to have been caused by military service. Family members may live elsewhere.
Select an area to see the issues it covers. Then select any issues you experienced. Answer from your own experience and, for family members, only from what you know.

pages.title: Your experience: {category_label}
pages.repeat: one complete page per priority category, at most two pages
intro: You selected the issues below. Think about the help you needed at the time, including help you received and help you did not receive.
All questions on this page are optional. A few words are enough. Each answer can be up to 10,000 characters. Leave any question that does not apply unanswered.
Please leave out identifying details. You may mention military support in general terms, but do not describe or rate internal military services.

questions.label: What kinds of help, if any, did you or your family need with these issues?
questions.help: Include help you received as well as help you needed but did not receive. You do not need to know which service could provide it.

sections.title: The needs that mattered most
sections.intro: You can tell us more about up to two needs. Use a separate set of answers for each need. You do not need to repeat your full answer above.
sections.repeat: one inline need entry per slot; one initially, up to two

questions.label: Which need would you like to tell us more about?
questions.help: Describe one of the needs that mattered most. Keep this same need in mind for the questions below.

sections.title: Sources of help
sections.repeat: once per present need slot, within this page

questions.label: Which of the issues you selected did you need this help with?
questions.help: You can describe the connection in your own words, or leave this blank if the need relates to the area more generally.
questions.show_when: more than one specific issue selected in this category

questions.label: For this need, where did you look for or receive help?
questions.help: Include attempts that did not lead to help, online information you used and help offered without asking. Describe the type of support, without identifying individual people. Mention military support only in general terms.

sections.title: Your experience of these sources of help

questions.label: What was your experience of trying to get or receiving help from services outside the military for these needs?
questions.help: You can describe what made getting or using help easier or harder. Where experiences differed, say which source or need you are describing. You can leave this blank if it does not apply.

questions.label: What influenced whether you used other sources of help outside the military for these needs?
questions.help: You can mention sources you knew about but did not use, or difficulties finding out what was available. You do not need to guess about services you do not know.

sections.title: Friends and family
sections.show_when: first current priority area; keep the same respondent-level answer if priorities change

questions.label: How would you describe your friends and family as a source of support?
questions.help: Think about your support network generally. You can describe what makes it easier or harder to get support from them. You do not need to have asked them for help.

sections.title: How well was this need met?
sections.repeat: once per present need slot, within this page

questions.label: How well did the help from each source outside the military meet this need?
questions.help: Include help from friends or family. You can describe different sources separately. Please distinguish receiving no help from receiving help that did not meet your need. Do not describe or rate internal military services.

questions.label: Overall, how fully was this need met?
questions.help: Think about all the help you received and anything you managed yourself. For an ongoing situation, answer about now. For a situation that ended, answer about how things stood when it ended. You do not need to describe internal military services.

questions.label: What help with this need, if any, are you or your family still missing now?
questions.help: You can explain what is still missing and what would make that support work for you.

questions.label: Is there anything else you would like us to understand about this need?
questions.help: Optional. You can explain what help you needed, what happened, what worked or what is still missing. Write as much or as little as you like, up to 10,000 characters. Please leave out identifying details and do not describe internal military services.

sections.title: Anything else you would like to add?
sections.show_when: no need slots remain, or an area comment was previously written

questions.label: Is there anything else you would like us to understand about these issues?
questions.help: Optional. You can tell us what has helped, what matters to you or what might help in the future. You do not need to repeat anything you have already written.

pages.title: Before you finish
intro: You can check your answers below and choose Edit to make changes. You do not need to repeat anything you have already told us.

sections.title: Anything else you would like to add?

questions.label: Is there anything else you would like us to understand about Defence life and support in Greater Darwin?
questions.help: Optional. You can mention issues not discussed in detail, support that helps your family stay well and connected, or help you may need in the coming months. Up to 10,000 characters. Please leave out identifying details and internal military service details.

pages.title: Thank you
intro: Thank you for sharing your experiences and ideas, and for helping to shape a stronger, more connected Defence community in Greater Darwin.

local_adaptations: Parallel alternative to the v4 choice questionnaire; no v4 file is replaced.
Welcome, demographics, issue bank, issue selection, category priorities, final review and thanks are inherited. Only What to expect is adjusted to describe written answers.
Needs summary is free text; up to two respondent-defined priority-need slots replace predefined H01–H11 choices. No automatic parsing or classification.
Every middle question is free text, including sources, source experiences, reasons for not using sources, personal support networks, helpfulness, overall fulfilment and current gaps.
Q32/Q33 concepts are covered by open prompts once per area, not their seven fixed statements or a complete source-type matrix. Source-specific distinctions must be explicit in the narrative.
The general personal-network question appears once on the first priority area rather than being gated by a source checkbox. No meaning is inferred from the source narrative.
Each middle answer has a separate optional 10000-code-point field. No open answer becomes a score or a closed response without a separate documented coding process.
